signTitle: Signs Your Dryer Vent May Need Cleaning
signIntro: Lint can collect inside your dryer's exhaust duct even when you clean the lint filter regularly. These warning signs can help you recognize when the vent may need attention.
signs: Laundry that used to dry in one cycle now needs another?
The dryer or laundry area becoming unusually hot during use?
Visible lint collecting behind the dryer or near the exhaust connection?
Little air coming from the exterior dryer vent while the dryer operates?
A burning smell, smoke, or unusual heat when the dryer runs? Stop using the dryer until the cause is checked.
Heavy lint, debris, or nesting material around the outdoor dryer vent opening?
workTitle: Dryer Vent Cleaning: What to Compare
workIntro: Dryer vent cleaning focuses on removing lint and loose debris from the exhaust path. Before-and-after photos should show the same components so homeowners can understand which areas were serviced.

processTitle: What Happens During Dryer Vent Cleaning?
processIntro: Santa Chimney Sweep evaluates the accessible dryer exhaust path and removes lint and loose debris from the areas included in the service. The cleaning approach depends on the vent configuration, duct materials, access, and buildup found.
steps: Our team begins by reviewing the problem you've noticed.
Longer drying times, unusual heat, visible lint, weak outdoor airflow, or suspected blockage help identify the areas that may need attention.
Technicians also review the known vent location and any access concerns before cleaning begins.
The dryer exhaust system includes the connection behind the appliance, the duct leading outdoors, and the exterior termination.
Technicians review the accessible sections relevant to the request.
They look for visible lint accumulation, loose debris, damaged connections, crushed duct sections, and other conditions that may restrict airflow.
Technicians use professional cleaning equipment suited to the accessible exhaust configuration to loosen and remove lint and loose debris from the areas included in the service.
The cleaning method depends on the duct route, bends, length, and available access points.
If the work requires moving or disconnecting the dryer, reaching a roof outlet, or addressing a difficult blockage, the required access and scope should be confirmed before proceeding.
After cleaning, technicians review the accessible sections covered by the service.
The team explains the areas addressed and any visible damage or remaining restriction requiring attention.
If the dryer continues to operate poorly after the vent has been cleaned, the appliance may need a separate evaluation.

optionsTitle: When Does Your Dryer Need More Than Vent Cleaning?
optionsIntro: Not every drying or airflow problem is caused by lint buildup. Some conditions require duct repair, appliance service, or a different type of cleaning.
options: Crushed or Damaged Exhaust Ducts
A crushed, kinked, disconnected, or deteriorated exhaust duct can restrict airflow or release exhaust into the wrong area.
Cleaning will not correct damaged duct materials or an improperly connected exhaust system.
The affected section may require repair or replacement.
Dryer Appliance Problems
Long drying times, overheating, or unusual dryer operation can also involve the appliance itself.
If the exhaust path has been cleaned but the problem continues, the dryer may need a qualified appliance technician.
Lint removal does not repair heating elements, motors, sensors, or other internal appliance components.
Difficult Exterior Vent Access
Some dryer vents terminate through the roof or another area that requires special access.
The location of the outlet can affect how the cleaning is completed and whether additional arrangements are necessary.
Confirm roof or difficult-access service availability before booking.
Bird Nests or Other Obstructions
Nesting material, debris, or a stuck exterior vent cover may block the exhaust outlet.
The appropriate response depends on the obstruction and the condition of the vent components.
Wildlife removal, damaged covers, or replacement work may require a service beyond routine lint cleaning.
Dust Inside Your Home's HVAC Ducts
Your dryer's exhaust duct and your home's heating and cooling ducts are different systems.
If the concern involves dust or debris inside supply or return air vents, residential air duct cleaning may be more appropriate.

standard: Cleaning Focused on the Exhaust Path
A dryer's lint filter, connecting duct, main exhaust run, and exterior outlet are different parts of the system.
Our team considers the reported concern and accessible vent configuration when reviewing the cleaning request.
The goal is to address the lint and debris within the approved service scope.
Homeowners can review which exhaust sections are included before cleaning begins.
The scope should distinguish ordinary lint removal from dryer disconnection, roof access, difficult blockages, and duct repairs when those require separate arrangements.
This helps establish what work will be performed during the appointment.
Dryer vent cleaning can remove accumulated lint and debris, but it does not guarantee that every drying problem will be corrected or that a future dryer fire cannot occur.
If technicians find damaged venting or believe the problem involves the dryer appliance, they explain the concern rather than automatically treating additional cleaning as the solution.

faq: How Do I Know If My Dryer Vent Is Clogged?
Longer drying times, weak airflow outside, visible lint around the vent, and unusual heat may indicate a restriction.
However, these problems can also involve the dryer itself.
If the dryer produces smoke or a burning smell, stop using it until the cause has been professionally evaluated.
Does Dryer Vent Cleaning Include the Outside Vent and Dryer Connection?
The exact service depends on your home's exhaust configuration and the approved cleaning scope.
Confirm whether the appointment includes the dryer-side connection, main exhaust duct, and exterior outlet.
If your dryer exhaust exits through the roof, mention this when booking so access and service availability can be confirmed.
How Often Should Dryer Vents Be Professionally Cleaned?
Annual professional cleaning is a common maintenance recommendation, although some systems may require attention sooner.
Dryer use, vent length, bends, and lint buildup can affect how often service is needed.
Clean the dryer's lint filter after each load and follow the manufacturer's maintenance instructions.
Read AHAM Clothes Dryer Safety Guidance

Can Dryer Vent Cleaning Reduce the Risk of a Dryer Fire?
Removing lint and loose debris helps address one of the conditions that can contribute to dryer fires.
The U.S. Fire Administration identifies failure to clean as a leading contributing factor in residential clothes dryer fires.
However, cleaning cannot eliminate every fire hazard. Damaged ductwork, appliance faults, and other problems may require separate attention.
Read U.S. Fire Administration Appliance Fire Safety Guidance
https://www.usfa.fema.gov/prevention/home-fires/prevent-fires/appliance-and-electrical/
What Information Should I Provide When Booking Dryer Vent Cleaning?
Tell us your dryer type, property ZIP code, and whether the vent exits through a wall or roof.
Mention longer drying times, unusual heat, burning smells, visible lint, or a suspected blockage.
You do not need to move or disconnect the dryer just to provide this information.
